title: The Story of the Star of Gladness
synopsis: What do traveling the world aboard a sailboat and learning Chinese have in common? This is the Advanced level winning text for our “Chinese Story” event, written by 邬乐.

fullText.simplified:
幸福之星号的故事

    你小的时候有梦想吗？我觉得很多人在他们小的时候都有大大的梦想，可是等他们长大以后，梦想却越来越小了。因为他们长大成人后，开始担心工作、房子、自己的孩子等各种各样的事情。不过我的妈妈，她没有放弃她的梦想。
    我的妈妈从小就热爱海洋。她住在夏威夷，所以每天下课以后都去游泳、冲浪、钓鱼。她最喜欢的是驾驶帆船航行，因此她的梦想就是住在一艘帆船上，环游世界。
    我六岁的时候，妈妈的梦想实现了。通过打工，她有了一些积蓄。于是，我们把房子租了出去，我们则搬出去，住到了船上。我妈妈叫它Hokulea，意思是“幸福之星号”，这是一个很有名的夏威夷船名。就这样，我和我的家人开始了我们的奇遇。
    我们从美国的康州出发，然后向北航行到加拿大，再向南航行到巴哈马。我们遇到其他驾船的人时，他们觉得我们很奇怪：船长竟然是一个女人——我的妈妈。然而他们不知道的是，我的妈妈是一名很优秀的船长。她还能钓鱼给我们吃，而且她的职业是医生，所以她知道怎么保证我们的健康。
    我们有很多很多的经历，有的很棒，有的很可怕。
    一天，我们在离麻省很近的海面上航行。那时风平浪静，所以帆船开得很慢，温度正好。妈妈说我和姐姐可以游泳。我们游来游去，很好玩儿！但就在我们从水里出来上到船上的时候，我们的小狗开始汪汪大叫。原来一条大白鲨就在我们帆船附近！
    在巴哈马，海的颜色很漂亮，看起来像一张风景画。可是那里浪很大，我们常常晕船……一天，海上的浪很大，而且没有风，所以我们不舒服了。妈妈说：“深呼吸，看看天边。”就在那时，五个海豚来到了我们的帆船前。它们跳舞、游泳，逗我们开心，让我们忘记了肚子的不舒服。
    在帆船上的那一年，尽管不容易，却教会了我们很多。
    我的妈妈教会了我：要有大梦想。当时，很多人都觉得她疯了：女人不可能做船长，一家人不可能在帆船上住一年！不过她没有放弃她的梦想。她的梦想教会了我：勇敢、忠诚、爱旅行，去认识与我完全不同的人。妈妈告诉我：“即使别人说你不可能完成你的目标、梦想，你也要相信你可以。”
    我的梦想呢？就是搬到中国，学习汉语。现在，我就在这儿！你的梦想是什么？
fullText.traditional:
幸福之星號的故事

    你小的時候有夢想嗎？我覺得很多人在他們小的時候都有大大的夢想，可是等他們長大以後，夢想卻越來越小了。因為他們長大成人後，開始擔心工作、房子、自己的孩子等各種各樣的事情。不過我的媽媽，她沒有放棄她的夢想。
    我的媽媽從小就熱愛海洋。她住在夏威夷，所以每天下課以後都去游泳、衝浪、釣魚。她最喜歡的是駕駛帆船航行，因此她的夢想就是住在一艘帆船上，環遊世界。
    我六歲的時候，媽媽的夢想實現了。通過打工，她有了一些積蓄。於是，我們把房子租了出去，我們則搬出去，住到了船上。我媽媽叫它Hokulea，意思是“幸福之星號”，這是一個很有名的夏威夷船名。就這樣，我和我的家人開始了我們的奇遇。
    我們從美國的康州出發，然後向北航行到加拿大，再向南航行到巴哈馬。我們遇到其他駕船的人時，他們覺得我們很奇怪：船長竟然是一個女人——我的媽媽。然而他們不知道的是，我的媽媽是一名很優秀的船長。她還能釣魚給我們吃，而且她的職業是醫生，所以她知道怎麼保證我們的健康。
    我們有很多很多的經歷，有的很棒，有的很可怕。
    一天，我們在離麻省很近的海面上航行。那時風平浪靜，所以帆船開得很慢，溫度正好。媽媽說我和姐姐可以游泳。我們游來游去，很好玩兒！但就在我們從水裡出來上到船上的時候，我們的小狗開始汪汪大叫。原來一條大白鯊就在我們帆船附近！
    在巴哈馬，海的顏色很漂亮，看起來像一張風景畫。可是那裡浪很大，我們常常暈船……一天，海上的浪很大，而且沒有風，所以我們不舒服了。媽媽說：“深呼吸，看看天邊。”就在那時，五個海豚來到了我們的帆船前。它們跳舞、游泳，逗我們開心，讓我們忘記了肚子的不舒服。
    在帆船上的那一年，儘管不容易，卻教會了我們很多。
    我的媽媽教會了我：要有大夢想。當時，很多人都覺得她瘋了：女人不可能做船長，一家人不可能在帆船上住一年！不過她沒有放棄她的夢想。她的夢想教會了我：勇敢、忠誠、愛旅行，去認識與我完全不同的人。媽媽告訴我：“即使別人說你不可能完成你的目標、夢想，你也要相信你可以。”
    我的夢想呢？就是搬到中國，學習漢語。現在，我就在這兒！你的夢想是什麼？

sentences.pinyin: tā de mèng xiǎng jiāo huì le wǒ yǒng gǎn zhōng chéng ài lǚ xíng qù rèn shi yǔ wǒ wán quán bù tóng de rén
sentences.english: But she never gave up on her dream.

sentences.simplified: 妈妈告诉我：“即使别人说你不可能完成你的目标、梦想，你也要相信你可以。”
sentences.traditional: 媽媽告訴我：“即使別人說你不可能完成你的目標、夢想，你也要相信你可以。”
sentences.pinyin: mā ma gào su wǒ jí shǐ bié ren shuō nǐ bù kě néng wán chéng nǐ de mù biāo mèng xiǎng nǐ yě yào xiāng xìn nǐ kě yǐ
sentences.english: Her dream taught me: courage, dedication, a love of traveling, and to meet people that are completely different than me.
Mom told me, “Even if other people say that you can’t achieve your goals and dreams, you need to believe that you can.”

sentences.simplified: 我的梦想呢？就是搬到中国，学习汉语。
sentences.traditional: 我的夢想呢？就是搬到中國，學習漢語。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de mèng xiǎng ne jiù shì bān dào zhōng guó xué xí hàn yǔ

sentences.simplified: 现在，我就在这儿！你的梦想是什么？
sentences.traditional: 現在，我就在這兒！你的夢想是什麼？
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài wǒ jiù zài zhè‘r nǐ de mèng xiǎng shì shén me
sentences.english: What’s my dream, then? It’s to move to China and study the Chinese language.
And now, I’m here! What’s your dream?

raw.synopsis: What do traveling the world aboard a sailboat and learning Chinese have in common? This is the Advanced level winning text for our “Chinese Story” event, written by 邬乐.
sentence_translations: The Story of the Star of Gladness
Did you have big dreams when you were little?
I feel as if a lot of people have big dreams when they’re little, ..
.. but after the grow up, their dreams become smaller and smaller.
Because after they grow up into adulthood, ..
.. they begin to worry about jobs, houses, their own children, and all sorts of things like that.
But my mom, she never gave up on her dreams.
My mom has loved the ocean since she was little.
She lived in Hawaii, so every day after school she would go swimming, surfing, and fishing.
Her favorite thing was piloting sailboats, because her dream was to live on a sailboat and travel the world.
When I was six years old, my mom’s dream came true.
She had accumulated some savings through casual jobs.
So, we rented out our house, and then we moved out of the house and onto a boat.
My mom called it Hokulea, which means “Star of Gladness”. This is a famous Hawaiian name for a boat.
Just like that, my family and I began our adventure.
We started from the U.S. state of Connecticut, sailed north to Canada, then sailed south to the Bahamas.
When we came across other sailors, they found us to be quite strange: our captain was actually a woman – my mom.
What they didn’t know was that my mom is an exceptional captain.
She could also catch fish for us to eat, ..
.. and she is a doctor by profession, so she knew how to ensure that we were all healthy.
We had many, many experiences; some of them were amazing and some of them were scary.
One day, we were sailing on waters very near Massachusetts.
At that time the wind was calm and the waves smooth, so we were sailing quite slowly.
The temperature was just right.
Mom said my older sister and I go could swimming.
We were swimming around and it was a lot of fun!
But just as we climbed out of the water back onto the boat, our dog began to bark very loudly.
It turns out a great white shark was near our boat!
In the Bahamas, the color of the ocean is very beautiful; it looks like a postcard.
But the waves there are very big and we’d often get seasick…
One day, the waves were really big and there was no wind, so we started feeling sick.
Mom said, “Take some deep breaths and look out at the horizon.”
Just then, five dolphins appeared in front of our sailboat.
Their dancing and swimming made us happy and forget about our upset stomachs.
That year aboard the sailboat, although it wasn’t easy, it taught us a lot.
My mom taught me this: dream big.
At the time, a lot of people thought she was crazy:
It wasn’t possible for a woman to be a captian, it wasn’t possible for a family to live aboard a sailboat for a year!
But she never gave up on her dream.
Her dream taught me: courage, dedication, a love of traveling, and to meet people that are completely different than me.
Mom told me, “Even if other people say that you can’t achieve your goals and dreams, you need to believe that you can.”
What’s my dream, then? It’s to move to China and study the Chinese language.
And now, I’m here! What’s your dream?
